on/toronto.title: Queen Street: choose the shop before choosing the bowl

decisions.title: Two nearby addresses, different stocks
decisions.text: Ikkousha at 249 Queen Street West uses the pork menu; 257 Queen Street West is the chicken shop. The Yonge–Dundas branch also links to the pork menu. A brand search alone can send you to the wrong menu, even when the bowl names look similar.

decisions.title: Compare the $16 baselines
decisions.text: Signature Tonkotsu at the pork shop and Tori Paitan at the chicken shop both cost $16. The one-dollar step to Black Tonkotsu or Tori Black changes the recipe within the chosen shop. A two-bowl baseline is $32 before extras; two black-garlic bowls are $34.

decisions.title: Separate fish, noodles and stock
decisions.text: Tori Gyokai combines chicken and fish. The chicken-shop label does not exclude seafood. Both menus offer a $2 dine-in gluten-free noodle substitution, while explicitly warning that the kitchen is not gluten-free. A noodle substitution is a different decision from a broth choice.

bc/vancouver.title: Vancouver: vegan menus, portion sizes and branch-only sides

decisions.title: A plant-based base without a surcharge
decisions.text: DANBO’s shared Vancouver menu prices regular Classic pork and Classic Vegan bowls at $12.95 each. For a mixed-diet pair, those two base bowls total $25.90. Use the separate vegan ordering path; adding the regular ramen egg changes the dietary suitability.

decisions.title: Let the side determine the branch
decisions.text: The same menu labels its plant-based bun Main Street only and fried rice Kerrisdale only. If a side is the reason for choosing DANBO, decide the branch before travelling. Shared ramen pricing does not imply that the whole side menu is shared.

decisions.title: Portion versus preparation at Gojiro
decisions.text: Gojiro’s Bakamori increases meat, noodles and toppings. Its tsukemen changes to a separate dipping soup instead. Those are two different ways to change a meal. The online page does not publish bowl prices, so Gojiro stays out of numeric budget comparisons until a price is confirmed.

ab/edmonton.title: Edmonton: compare the stock and the topping separately

decisions.title: The chicken-stock substitution
decisions.text: Tokiwa’s Chuka Soba costs $16 but normally includes pork chashu. The listed chicken substitution adds $2, making an $18 base order. Shiawase’s Chicken Shoyu is $18.50 with chicken stock and chicken chashu. The useful comparison is $18 versus $18.50, not the two headline soup prices.

decisions.title: Tofu does not settle the recipe
decisions.text: Shiawase now lists Mapo Tofu Ramen at $18.50, and its description explicitly includes minced pork. Its $22.95 brothless mazemen contains pork, egg and fish powder. Neither name should be used as a vegetarian shortcut.

decisions.title: A group budget has extra conditions
decisions.text: Tokiwa states cash or debit, no split bills, and an automatic 18% gratuity for six or more. Six $16 bowls are a $96 food subtotal; 18% of that subtotal is $17.28. Confirm how the restaurant calculates its final bill before using that illustration for a group.

ab/calgary.title: Calgary: two $17 orders with very different ingredients

decisions.title: Brothless is not plant-based
decisions.text: At Goro + Gun, Vegan Mushroom and Mazemen both cost $17. The first is explicitly vegan; the second contains onsen egg and BBQ pork. A pair of either costs $34 before extras, so the decision is about format and ingredients rather than base price.

decisions.title: Chicken soup can carry pork
decisions.text: Globefish Chinook’s Miso, Paitan and Kuro Garlic descriptions use chicken soup with pork chashu. Its separately named Vegan Creamy is the clear plant-based choice. Do not carry a broth preference over to the topping without checking both.

decisions.title: Price the extra noodles deliberately
decisions.text: Goro + Gun lists extra noodles at $4. A $17 Vegan Mushroom base plus extra noodles is $21 before other charges, while its $19 Smoked Brisket is a different recipe at a lower subtotal. Compare the meal you want, not an assumed ranking by price; ask about noodle ingredients for dietary needs.

on/guelph.title: Guelph: compare Crafty’s bowl upgrade with its combo

decisions.title: Seasoning at the same base price
decisions.text: Crafty’s Tokyo Salaryman and Big City Smoke both start at $16.85. The first follows shoyu seasoning; the second follows miso. Both offer choices that pair a protein with a stock. Choosing tofu changes that pairing, but is not independent proof about every ingredient.

decisions.title: Two ways to spend around $20
decisions.text: Tokyo Salaryman plus the $2.50 combo is $19.35, including a half snack and a pop. Meat Lover 2.0 alone is $20.85. The $1.50 difference compares an add-on combination with a more elaborate bowl; it does not establish equal portions or a universal better deal.

decisions.title: Restaurant and freezer menus differ
decisions.text: Use the menu attached to 17 Macdonell Street for this plan. Frozen products on the same website are a separate purchase. The October check no longer shows the chilled Redeye or Kimchi Mazemen from our earlier capture, so those are excluded from the current bowl selector.

mb/winnipeg.title: Winnipeg: compare named recipes rather than protein labels

decisions.title: A chicken topping over mixed stock
decisions.text: Gaijin’s Spicy Chicken Karaage Ramen is $17.50, but the described broth contains both pork and chicken. Its $16.50 Miso uses the same two stock ingredients. Changing the topping or choosing the lower price does not remove pork from the soup.

decisions.title: An upgrade can close the price gap
decisions.text: Cho Ichi lists Shoyu at $17.50 and extra noodles at $3: $20.50 together. Its Original bowl is $21.50. That one-dollar gap is a reason to compare included ingredients and appetite before adding noodles automatically; the two orders are not equivalent portions.

decisions.title: Read the full Tan Tan description
decisions.text: Gaijin’s $17.50 Tan Tan explicitly includes peanuts and a pork-and-chicken stock. The $15.50 Vegetarian Ramen is labelled vegetarian, which does not establish vegan preparation. Use the exact recipe wording for a shortlist and ask the kitchen about essential dietary requirements.

sk/regina.title: Regina: the vegetarian bowl is a separate recipe

decisions.title: Three $19 directions
decisions.text: Dojo’s Shoyu, Miso and Spicy bowls are each $19 and list pork broth and pork belly. Soy seasoning, miso and heat distinguish the choices without changing the base price. Two bowls from that group total $38 before additions.

decisions.title: Vegetarian includes an egg
decisions.text: Dojo’s $21 Vegetarian Ramen lists a farm egg. It is $2 above the other three bowls, or a $4 increase for two. Removing meat from a preference filter is insufficient to turn the default recipe into a vegan order.

decisions.title: Pronto pricing needs a new check
decisions.text: Pronto’s homepage still exposes its hours, but the full menu was not readable during the October source check. Its older menu snapshot remains dated below. We exclude that snapshot from price-ceiling calculations until the current prices can be confirmed.
